summary: Feed s159_double to NDR is degraded: 26.3% duplicate packets (high) will skew NDR analytics, and encrypted traffic at 91.7% slightly exceeds the NDR's 90% tolerance, limiting payload inspection. No drops, overload, one-way, or VLAN issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Duplicate delivery from aggregated SPAN/mirror sessions or dual TAP feeds combined on packet broker without deduplication - same packets arriving via two paths and forwarded twice to tool port. 1085 of 4127 packets (26.3%) are identical, well above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate processing, inflates flow/connection counts, distorts behavioral analytics and can cause false positives or missed detections due to skewed state tracking.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication on this feed to drop identical packets within a short time window before delivery to the NDR, restoring accurate traffic counts without losing unique flows.

findings.root_cause: 92% of bytes are encrypted (TLS), just above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic mix is predominantly encrypted with little cleartext payload available for deep inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection; with 91.7% encrypted it is largely blind to payload-based threats and must rely on metadata/flow analysis only, reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: NDR cannot inspect encrypted payloads natively. Advise enabling selective TLS decryption via SSL visibility appliance or packet broker decryption, or supplement with decrypted feed/metadata enrichment; do not filter encrypted traffic as NDR still needs flow metadata.
